title: I built an entire quant trading firm on Claude. 6 agents, each one has a job.

recreating.summary: @raycfu · "AI agent trading firm" · https://www.instagram.com/p/DcuOeJ4vmde/ · 2,346 likes and 3,867 comments on a 268K-follower account

length: about 66s at Joshua's pace, fast, no pauses between lines (the original is 40s) · Presenter: Joshua

lines.text: Most people don't realize that someone just built an entire Wall Street trading firm with AI agents.
You give the system a single stock ticket and the entire AI trading floor goes to work.
Here's how you build it out.
Four specialized analyst agents dig into the data, analyze company fundamentals, breaking market news, track social sentiment, and prize action.
A bull and bear agent debate both sides of the trade against each other in order to challenge the hidden risk.
Then a trader agent plans the execution, but a separate risk management agent has the power to veto the move before the portfolio management agent signs it off.
The best part is the system has persistent memory.
Every trader recommendation gets graded and logged against actual market results so the agents study their own mistakes and improve over time.
I put together a complete setup guide on how to build this out for yourself with the GitHub repo link.
If you want it, just like the video and comment firm and I'll send it to you.
Follow for my ways to make money and run your business with tech and AI.

notes: **Recreating:** @raycfu · https://www.instagram.com/p/DcuOeJ4vmde/ · copy its rhythm: a UI insert in the top third from about 3s, changing about every 2s; a punch-in between wide and close-up at every new beat (line 2, line 5, line 7's "but", line 11's "The best part"); one agent per line, each with its own card; the risk manager's red "NO" card as the twist; the CTA over a close-up.

**Layout:** split screen. Insert in the top third (1080×640), Joshua below, filmed wide; punch-ins (110%) and close-ups (130%) come from the same take. Captions 1–3 words at chest height, key words in gold #E8B04B. Our own style (dark #0B0F14 cards, gold), not raycfu's serif titles or his UI cards.

**The org chart** (A1) is the thread: 6 grey boxes in a row of 3 over a row of 3. On the word each agent is named, A1 (1080×360) shows for 1s, centred in the top third on dark #0B0F14, with that box lighting up. Then cut to that agent's recording, full width in the top third (1080×640, scaled to fit width, centred), with A1 hidden. A1 comes back on the next agent's name. Exception: on lines 8–10, the red A1 (8) sits at the top of the top third, and the rule cards A7 (1)–(3) (1080×280) sit directly under it, filling the rest. Each box turns gold on the word its agent is named, and stays gold. The risk manager box turns red on line 7 and green on line 12's "yes".
**Times** are estimates at 3 words a second (about 70s); Joshua reads about 3.2, so the take runs about 66s. Re-time to the real take.

notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.
**Before recording anything:** the Qube team connects Claude to Qube on Joshua's laptop and gives him a Qube login. Don't show any install commands, API keys, emails, account numbers or file paths.

**Before A2 (the six agents):** Joshua (or the Qube team) checks that the six agents exist in that Claude session with these jobs: research (news and earnings on the ticker), data (up to five years of price data), strategy (builds it in Qube), backtest (tests it in Qube), risk manager (says no to any trade risking more than 2% of the account, stops trading for the day at the max loss, says no if the backtest doesn't hold up), trader (simulation account only for this video). If any are missing, tell Mark before recording.
**Recording order for the laptop clips** (one run, they build on each other): A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → A8 → A9. All in one Claude session, recording the whole run, then cut into the clips below.
**The example ticker is NVDA.** It's only an example input, never a call: no "buy" anywhere next to it, and "Example" under it on screen.

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure. 2. Frame wide (head and chest), and leave the top third of the frame empty above his head (the screens go there). 3. Record the hook twice, clean. 4. Record lines 1–15 in one take, fast, no pauses between lines. 5. Move the phone in close (face fills the frame) and record, three times each: "Here's how I built it out." · "but a separate risk manager has the power to say no." · "The best part is what happens when the risk manager says no." · "Comment QUBE and I'll send you the link for the free sign-up."

Keep recording while the strategy agent fixes the strategy and the backtest agent tests it again, round after round. 3. Hold 2s on the risk manager's "yes". 4. Take one screenshot of the "no" and one of the "yes". 5. Tell the editor how many rounds it took (the "ROUND" counter only goes that high). **CHECK: the risk manager must really say no, then yes, in this run. If it says yes the first time, stop and tell Mark. Lines 10–12 need a real no; never stage one. The 'no' must be the risk manager's backtest reason (the backtest doesn't hold up). If it says no for a different reason, send Mark the screenshot before the edit.**

open.text: **"Simulation account" vs the badge.** The spoken line says "simulation account" (your J022 wording). The `finance-compliance` badge on A9 reads "Paper trading · simulated results". Kept as written until you answer P1 in `data/mark-edits/proposals.md`.
**The real "no" (A8).** Lines 10–12 only work if the risk manager says no and then yes in the run you record. If your run says yes on the first try, we need to decide before the edit.
**Example ticker.** NVDA is set as the example input (A2). Say if you'd rather use a different one; it's only typed, never called a buy.
**A2 step 4.** The Qube team names the exact command or screen that shows Qube connected in Claude (no keys or file paths in shot). Until then, step 4 can't be filmed.
**Strategy sections (A5).** The four on-screen chips ("WHEN TO BUY" "WHEN TO SELL" "HOW MUCH" "WHEN TO GET OUT") follow Qube's section names; if Qube shows different names, the chips change to match.
